why: The AUTHORED half of a feature-ledger row. l6-parity-rows.cjs derives every MEASURED field from a cat6 run artifact and refuses to invent any of these; a spec row id with no entry here refuses BY NAME rather than being written with a guessed route. One block per app, keyed by the row ids in probes/l6-parity.js.
howToAddAnApp: Read the app.s SPECS block in probes/l6-parity.js for its row ids, then write one entry per id. The two destination strings and noLiquidReason are per-app, not per-row.

provenance.dictionary: Copied MECHANICALLY out of the seven dictionary rows already in parity-ledger.json (written by hand on 2026-08-17), in the spec.s own id order, by a one-off node read of the ledger -- not retyped. CORRECTED 2026-09-02: this note used to claim the seventh row, "Window lifecycle: pop out, minimize, maximize, close", had NO spec id and was "deliberately absent". That was false -- `l6-parity.js` declares `{ id: 'windowLifecycle', f: lifecycle }` for every app, and the live run refused BY NAME on it, which is the refusal working. Its four authored fields are now copied from that same ledger row. This block is a REGRESSION TEST -- a live cat6 dictionary run must re-derive these SEVEN features and add ZERO new rows, because the ledger already holds them under the same app-plus-feature keys. Measured 2026-09-02 at 1ec440ab: 7 rows, statuses {both: 7}, added 0.
provenance.calendar: AUTHORED 2026-09-02 from source, and it is the first app whose block was NOT back-derived from an existing ledger row -- parity-ledger.json had no calendar row at all, so all five are new and `added` is expected to be 5, not 0. Every `currentRoute` names the selector the spec.s own `f()` reads, so the authored half cannot drift from the measured half without the run failing. `dataStateOwner` read from src/renderer/calendar.ts (LS_KEYS.calendarEvents in localStorage, mirrored to IDB_KEYS.calendarEvents) and CalendarContent.tsx (mode / cursor / modal are component state, not persisted). Liquid destination read from calendarLiquid.css and the two LiquidSurface call sites at CalendarContent.tsx:391 and :403.
provenance.settings: AUTHORED 2026-09-02 from source, second app with no prior ledger row -- all seven are new. Every currentRoute names the selector the spec.s own f() reads. dataStateOwner separates persisted from not: advancedDisclosure is the only settings row here that survives a reopen (renderer/settingsAdvanced.ts, localStorage jp-settings-advanced-v1), while page, query and scroll are component state. Liquid destination read from the ContextualSurface call sites in SettingsNav.tsx (45, 46, 65, 69) and SettingsApp.tsx:604, and from the pane at SettingsApp.tsx:596-600 which is NOT wrapped.
provenance.scraper: AUTHORED 2026-09-02 from source, third app with no prior ledger row -- all seven are new. Every currentRoute names the selector the spec's own f() reads, so the authored half cannot drift from the measured half without the run failing. dataStateOwner separates the two localStorage documents this app owns: the SHELL shape (page, rail, drawerOpen, drawerCategory) in renderer/scraperShellStore.ts under jp-scraper-shell-v1, and the SETTINGS values in renderer/scraperSettingsStore.ts under jp-scraper-settings-v1. reverseControls is authored against the DISCLOSURE, not against aria-pressed, because the aria-pressed reading was a measured false positive fixed in ddeb97f3: with the drawer shut and advanced mode on, the old expression counted the button labelled "Advanced controls shown" (1) and scored a reversal affordance that is not on screen. Liquid destination read from the ContextualSurface call sites in ScraperTopBar.tsx:18, ScraperNav.tsx:22/34/42/53, ScraperStatusBar.tsx:25 and ScraperSettingsDrawer.tsx:248, and from the AnchorSurface anchors at ScraperSearch.tsx:89 and ScraperSettingsDrawer.tsx:261/:319.
provenance.resources: AUTHORED 2026-09-02 from source, fourth app with no prior ledger row. SEVEN of its eight rows were written; `collectedSections` was DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN and its metadata entry is kept anyway so a later profile with collected tools writes it without re-authoring. The reason is a repair in the same commit: its mutation targets `.mytool-card .mytool-remove` and nothing is collected on this profile, so the mutation REFUSED rather than ran. cat6 used to score that identically to a mutation that ran and flipped the wrong row, which VOIDed a run whose other 7 mutations were exact; it now reports `armed: false` and `l6-parity-rows.cjs` skips exactly that row by name. Discriminating control, live: an ARMED-but-wrong mutation (catalogueCount re-pointed at `.res-name`, which flips `resourceCards` instead) still VOIDs the whole run, so the relaxation cannot wave a broken control through. dataStateOwner is three different owners here and they are not interchangeable: the catalogue is a STATIC module (renderer/data/resources.ts), the bundle checklists are localStorage under `resources.checklist.<id>`, and the collected tools are a MAIN-PROCESS store reached through window.api.toolsList (shared/collectedTools.ts), shared with Blanc. Liquid destination read from resourcesLiquid.css, whose `:is(.fwin.fwin-liquid, .popout-root.popout-liquid)` rules touch only `.res-command-surface` and its children.

viewModes.feature: Switch view mode: Month / Week / Day / Agenda
viewModes.currentRoute: Calendar window > `.cal-mode-btn` x4 in the `.cal-context-toolbar` mode row
viewModes.dataStateOwner: component state (`mode`) in CalendarContent.tsx — not persisted, so a reopen returns to Month

monthGrid.feature: Month grid: seven day-of-week headers over a full 42-cell numbered month
monthGrid.currentRoute: Calendar window > `.cal-month-grid` > `.cal-month-dow` x7 + `.cal-month-cell` x42, each carrying a `.cal-month-daynum`
monthGrid.keyboardRoute: cells are click targets; no keyboard grid navigation is claimed here

dateTransport.feature: Move through time: previous / today / next, plus a direct date jump
dateTransport.currentRoute: Calendar window > `.cal-nav` > three buttons + `input[type="date"]`, with the period named in `.cal-header-label`
dateTransport.keyboardRoute: three real buttons and a native date input
dateTransport.dataStateOwner: component state (the cursor date) in CalendarContent.tsx

eventComposer.feature: Create an event: the new-event composer and its cancel recovery
eventComposer.currentRoute: Calendar window > `.calendar-context-head > .btn` opens `.cal-modal`; `.cal-modal-actions` carries save and cancel
eventComposer.keyboardRoute: trigger is a real `type="button"`; the modal is a form of native inputs, selects and a textarea

windowLifecycle.feature: Window lifecycle: pop out, minimize, maximize, close

settings.standardDestination: SettingsApp in-window: the category rail on the left, the page pane (`role="main"`) on the right
settings.liquidDestination: Same in-window SettingsApp on the liquid material — `.fwin-liquid` + `data-presentation="liquid"`. SELECTIVE: the whole category rail is `ContextualSurface` (SettingsNav.tsx:45, :46, :65, :69) and so is the page header (SettingsApp.tsx:604), while `.os-set-pane-v2` itself stays a plain opaque body — a settings page is a form, and L2 keeps forms on stable anchors

categoryRail.feature: Category rail: the only route to 18 of the 19 settings pages
categoryRail.currentRoute: Settings window > `.os-set-nav-item`, each carrying both a visible label and a `title` (the label is clipped below 420px of `.os-set-body`, so `title` is the narrow tier's only text)
categoryRail.keyboardRoute: real buttons; the current one publishes `aria-current="page"`
categoryRail.dataStateOwner: the item set is derived from settingsRegistry.ts; which one is current is component state (`page`, SettingsApp.tsx:131) and is not persisted

groupedNavigation.feature: Grouped navigation: labelled groups, each list wired to its own label
groupedNavigation.keyboardRoute: each list is a labelled region a screen reader can enumerate; the items inside are buttons
groupedNavigation.dataStateOwner: group membership is declared per entry in settingsRegistry.ts

settingsSearch.feature: Settings search — the second route in, and the one the command palette uses
settingsSearch.currentRoute: Settings window > `.os-set-search-input`, `aria-controls` naming its result panel and `aria-expanded` a real boolean
settingsSearch.keyboardRoute: text input; Escape closes the panel synchronously
settingsSearch.dataStateOwner: `searchSettings()` over settingsRegistry.ts (SettingsSearch.tsx:12); the query itself is component state and is cleared on close

advancedDisclosure.feature: Advanced mode: show or hide the advanced pages, with the rail agreeing with the claim
advancedDisclosure.currentRoute: Settings window > `.os-set-advanced-btn` (`aria-pressed`), advanced rail entries marked by `.os-set-adv-dot`
advancedDisclosure.keyboardRoute: a real toggle button carrying `aria-pressed` and a `title`
advancedDisclosure.dataStateOwner: renderer/settingsAdvanced.ts — persisted in localStorage under `jp-settings-advanced-v1`; UI unlock only, background systems run either way

pageRegion.feature: The page pane names itself after the destination the rail says is current
pageRegion.keyboardRoute: a `main` landmark, reachable by landmark navigation
pageRegion.dataStateOwner: component state (`page`) in SettingsApp.tsx; the label is derived from the same value the rail renders, which is what makes a stale name detectable

homeOverview.feature: Home overview: status chips with real values, and quick cards that are working destinations
homeOverview.currentRoute: Settings window > Home > `.os-set-status-chip` (value in `strong`, caption in `.muted`) + `.os-set-quick-card` (SettingsHome.tsx:69ff, :162)
homeOverview.dataStateOwner: chips read live app state; the cards navigate through the same `page` state the rail uses

windowLifecycle.feature: Window lifecycle: pop out, minimize, maximize, close

scraper.standardDestination: Scraper window: `.scr-topbar` header, `.scr-rail` left navigation, the routed page body, `.scr-statusbar` footer, and the settings drawer that slides over the body when opened from the top bar
scraper.liquidDestination: Same in-window Scraper shell on the liquid material — `.fwin-liquid` + `data-presentation="liquid"`. SELECTIVE, not universal: the top bar (ScraperTopBar.tsx:18), the whole rail (ScraperNav.tsx:22/34/42/53) and the status bar (ScraperStatusBar.tsx:25) are `ContextualSurface` chrome, while the shell search (ScraperSearch.tsx:89) and the drawer's own search and field list (ScraperSettingsDrawer.tsx:261, :319) are `AnchorSurface bare` — a form of ~40 editable controls is work, and L2 keeps work on stable opaque anchors

railNavigation.feature: Reach every Scraper page from the left rail, with the current page marked and every item named
railNavigation.currentRoute: Scraper window > `.scr-rail-item` (17 buttons across grouped `.scr-rail-list`s), the active one carrying `aria-current="page"`
railNavigation.keyboardRoute: real `type="button"` list items inside `ul`/`li` with `aria-labelledby` group headings; `title` carries the label when the rail is collapsed and the description when it is not (ScraperNav.tsx:63)
railNavigation.dataStateOwner: renderer/scraperShellStore.ts — `navigateScraperShell` writes `page` (and the MRU `recentPages`) into localStorage `jp-scraper-shell-v1`, so the page survives a reopen

drawerCategories.feature: Settings drawer: pick a settings category and see its fields
drawerCategories.currentRoute: Scraper window > top-bar settings disclosure opens `.scr-drawer`; `.scr-drawer-rail > .scr-drawer-cat` x19, the active one carrying `aria-current="true"`, over `.scr-field` rows
drawerCategories.keyboardRoute: real `type="button"` category buttons; category clicks are wrapped in `startTransition` so the click paints before the page behind the drawer re-renders (ScraperSettingsDrawer.tsx:289)
drawerCategories.dataStateOwner: renderer/scraperShellStore.ts — `drawerOpen` and `drawerCategory` are fields of the same persisted `jp-scraper-shell-v1` document, so a reopened window comes back to the category you left

settingsFields.feature: Every settings field is a labelled control, never a bare input
settingsFields.keyboardRoute: native inputs, selects, toggles and range pairs inside a labelled row
settingsFields.dataStateOwner: renderer/scraperSettingsStore.ts — localStorage `jp-scraper-settings-v1`, a per-site document with presets; `getActiveScraperSettings(site)` is what the rest of the app reads

shellSearch.feature: Shell search: a combobox over pages and recent queries, collapsed until used
shellSearch.currentRoute: Scraper window > `.scr-search > .scr-search-input`, `role="combobox"` with `aria-controls="scr-search-results"` and `aria-expanded` reflecting the popover (ScraperSearch.tsx:104-113)
shellSearch.keyboardRoute: native `type="search"` input; the popover is a composite with the field, so focus moving to a result keeps it open and focus leaving it dismisses it (ScraperSearch.tsx:93-99)
shellSearch.dataStateOwner: component state (`query`, `open`) in ScraperSearch.tsx; the recent-query list comes from renderer/components/scraper/scraperRecent.ts and is the only persisted part

statusActions.feature: Status bar: run state, selection, last scrape and next schedule, each a route into the page that explains it
statusActions.currentRoute: Scraper window > `.scr-statusbar button` — the run-state button plus the last-scrape and next-schedule fields (and a selection button when a selection exists), every one carrying a `title`
statusActions.dataStateOwner: derived — job counts from ScraperApp state (`dashboardJobActive` / `transientJobActive`), last scrape and next schedule from the scraper history and schedule data the pages read

reverseControls.feature: Every drawer the shell opens can be closed again, from a control that says it is open
reverseControls.currentRoute: Scraper window > `.scr-drawer-head .ui-icon-btn` (the drawer's own close) and the top-bar disclosure at ScraperTopBar.tsx:78-86, which carries `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls` rather than `aria-pressed`
reverseControls.keyboardRoute: two real buttons; the disclosure is the APG pattern, so a screen reader announces the drawer as expanded rather than as a pressed toggle
reverseControls.dataStateOwner: renderer/scraperShellStore.ts — `drawerOpen` in `jp-scraper-shell-v1`; closing is a `patch({ drawerOpen: false })`, the exact inverse of opening

windowLifecycle.feature: Window lifecycle: pop out, minimize, maximize, close

resources.standardDestination: ResourcesContent in-window: the `.res-command-surface` command strip on top (heading, catalogue search, filter chips, visible-count line), then the landing sections (learner heat map, bundles, New, My tools) and the per-category `.res-group` catalogue below

categoryRail.feature: Filter the catalogue by category, with every rendered group offered as a chip
categoryRail.currentRoute: Resources window > `.res-filter .gram-level-btn` chips, exactly one carrying `active`, over the `.res-group .res-group-head h2` headings they filter to
categoryRail.keyboardRoute: real buttons in the command strip
categoryRail.dataStateOwner: component state (`filter`) in ResourcesContent.tsx over the static `renderer/data/resources.ts` catalogue — not persisted, so a reopen returns to All

catalogueCount.feature: The visible-count line equals what is actually painted

catalogueCount.keyboardRoute: not a control; it is the surface's own claim about the filtered catalogue

resourceCards.feature: Every catalogue card names itself, says which of free/paid/freemium it is, names the host it opens, and marks itself external

bundleGrid.feature: Curated bundles, each with its gem, title, link count and a checklist that cannot claim more ticks than it holds
bundleGrid.keyboardRoute: bundle cards are real buttons; the detail view is reachable and reversible
bundleGrid.dataStateOwner: bundle definitions are static; the per-bundle checklist is localStorage under the `resources.checklist.<bundleId>` prefix (ResourcesContent.tsx:49-63), which is why a stale list is the fabricated-progress case this row guards

collectedSections.feature: The two OPTIONAL landing strips — My tools and New — render nothing rather than an empty heading, and a collected tool always carries its remove control

collectedSections.keyboardRoute: remove is a real `IconButton`; the New strip is a native `<details>` disclosure

learnerHeatMap.feature: Learners-by-country greeting whose caption count equals the countries actually painted
learnerHeatMap.currentRoute: Resources window > `.heatmap-section` > `.heatmap-caption` over either `.heatmap-svg path` (choropleth) or `.heatmap-bar-row` (bars, each `.heatmap-bar-fill` width being its share of the largest)
